messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Canary alert triggered for release v2.4.1 (deploy-87). Healthcheck failing on 3/5 canary pods; 5xx rate 12% (> 5% abort threshold). Auto-abort criteria met. Marking thread for on-call.
ops-bot: deploy-87 details: image=redwood/model-server:v2.4.1, region=us-east-1, canary=5 pods, rollout start=03:05:20 UTC. Logs bucket: s3://redwood-logs/deploy-87/
alex: ack, oncall here. Pulling logs and canary metrics now. Paging release-engineering and SRE. @jess @sam please standby.
jess: oncall noted. I pushed the deploy. If abort went through, we should see traffic cut by the router. I can run the kill-switch unless we want a full rollback.
sam: looking at the metrics — CPU normal, latency up a bit, but 5xx is coming from one code path in model-serving. Repro locally might take a bit.
alex: can we flip the feature flag first to stop new traffic? Safer to close surface area while we decide rollback.
jess: feature flag for v2-serving is flippable. Command: 
```
redwood-ctl flags set v2-serving.enabled false --env production --scope canary
```
That will stop routing new requests to canary variant.
alex: running the flag now.
alex: `> redwood-ctl flags set v2-serving.enabled false --env production --scope canary` -- returned 200. Router should drain soon. Watching connection counts.
sam: running quick curl against problem endpoint on pod canary-03 to confirm 5xx stacktrace:
```
curl -sv http://canary-03.internal.redwood:8080/api/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
```
Response: 502 with JSON: {"error":"kv-cache-miss: shard 4 timeout"}
ops-bot: Noted: canary-03 shows repeated KV cache timeouts. Pod logs: /deploy-87/canary-03/serve.log -> see repeated 'shard 4: connection refused' entries.
tina: support queue: small set of customers hitting 5xx for the last ~2m. No major production-wide blast yet but we should be cautious. Tickets 1174, 1175 opened.
alex: since flag flip is applied, new sessions should be routed away. We should still rollback the canary to be safe. Jess, can you initiate rollback for deploy-87 canary group?
jess: doing rollback now. Command:
```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/model-server --to-revision=86
```
And then I'll update the router to point canary traffic to stable.
ops-bot: rollback job started at 03:07:45 UTC. kube events show pods terminating.
alex: paging note: PD incident created (PD-3412) and acknowledged by oncall. Severity set to P2 given canary abort and customer reports.
sam: after rollback started, canary pods now 0/5 ready. Monitoring 5xx: trending down to baseline ~0.6% in last 30s.
jess: rollback completed, cluster state reconciled. I also confirmed router rules reverted. Please monitor traces for slow tail.
alex: confirmed: healthcheck endpoints pass on all canary nodes after rollback. No new 5xx for 45s.
tina: support updated customers in tickets 1174/1175 that we rolled back and are monitoring. No further escalations.
alex: adding short postmortem task: capture root cause (kv-shard connection handling) + repro steps + mitigation (fix to cache client). Assigning to @sam and @jess. Will handoff to morning oncall for follow-up.
jess: will create deploy rollback playbook note and add a healthcheck regression test to CI.
sam: I'll collect logs and KV client traces and open a bug with reproducer. If anyone sees 5xx spike again, re-open this thread.
incident-bot: Incident PD-3412 updated: status=mitigated, mitigation=rollback to rev 86 and feature flag disabled for canary, owner=alex. Please close when postmortem created.
alex: thanks team. Leaving monitoring up for 30m, then handoff. :white_check_mark:
